title: Three Evenings and One Short Column
subtitle: 网络信息 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）
meta: 主题语境：网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）　|　核心词汇：headline　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 headline 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1996 the editor ① wrote the headline that no reader in the newsroom would have described, and he said the writing was the whole of the evening. The ② headline, meaning the title itself and not the column, ran three evenings and stayed undescribed in the book; a headline, he said, is the only thing in a newsroom that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ headline in that newsroom had the same short column beside it, and the ④ headline at the far screen, meaning the story they kept for the children to read and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A headline, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the editor said the describing is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the headline was the whole of the matter, meaning the spotlight and not the title. The ⑥ headline, meaning the spotlight and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; headline, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a title and a spotlight. He said the spotlight is the part they remember.

By 2001 the ⑦ headline had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short column. The ⑧ headline of the whole thing, the editor wrote in October, was one newsroom and three evenings of describing; headline, he said, is either the story at the far screen or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ headline I remember is the title described in the file, which closed in 2003 and is still described as the quietest in the newsroom. A ⑩ headline, my mother said in 2005, is the only title that improves by being described; every headline, she said, is a spotlight that has agreed to look like a title. She said the spotlight was the honest half.

headline 意为“标题”，指那条标题本身而不是栏目，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被描述。
headline 意为“标题”，指编辑室里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一道窄窄的短栏。
headline 意为“标题”，指最远那块屏幕留给孩子们读的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
headline 意为“关注、轰动”，指一件事里人人都写却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这阵轰动就是那件事的全部。
headline 意为“轰动”，指人人都写却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条标题，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
headline 意为“标题”，指卷宗里写到、被记下的的那一条，到 2001 年这一条成了卷宗里的一行。
headline 意为“题事”，编辑十月写道，整件事的标题之事是一处编辑室和三个夜晚的描述。
headline 意为“标题”，我记得的是卷宗里描述过的那一条，2003 年撤下了，至今仍被说成编辑室里最安静的一条。
headline 为抽象总称，母亲 2005 年说，标题是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的标题。
